records.title: Uncovering a clostridial toxin behind necrotizing enterocolitis
records.description: In a recent study, Zhang and colleagues identify Delta toxin produced by Clostridium perfringens as the driver of intestinal and brain injury in a subset of necrotizing enterocolitis.

records.title: The soil microbiome in an era of global change
records.description: Soils and their microbiomes are being severely affected by rapid global change. Understanding the effects of anthropogenic stressors on the soil microbiome is therefore key to improving soil resilience and ensuring planetary health. This Focus issue highlights the pressing threats to belowground microbial biodiversity and the opportunities and challenges to restore it.

records.title: The small intestine microbiome: composition, host interactions and therapeutic potential
records.description: In this Review, Britton and colleagues examine the composition of the small intestinal microbiome and its interactions with the host, highlighting emerging insights into its roles in physiology and health. They also discuss the challenges of studying this understudied microbial community and its potential as a source of future microbial therapeutics.

records.title: The microbiome’s voyage beyond Earth
records.description: This Genome Watch discusses how spaceflights affect microbiome composition and dynamics, highlighting how integrating metabolic and host data with microbiome monitoring could support astronaut health during long-term deep-space missions.

records.title: The mammalian archaeome: diversity, function and emerging roles in health and disease
records.description: In this Review, Moissl-Eichinger and colleagues explore the distribution, diversity and function of the mammalian archaeome, with a focus on humans and ruminants. They explore the ecological and physiological roles of Methanobrevibacter spp. as key gastrointestinal colonizers, the archaeal interactions with bacterial communities and the host, and the impact of health and disease on the human archaeome.

records.title: The contextual pathogenicity of Porphyromonas gingivalis
records.description: In this Review, Lamont and Hajishengallis explore how the pathogenicity of Porphyromonas gingivalis is determined by microbial, metabolic and host context. They discuss how community interactions, nutrient-sensing and immune subversion regulate virulence and drive dysbiosis, inflammation and periodontitis progression.

records.title: Global change reshapes marine microbial communities, functions and One Health outcomes
records.description: Global change is transforming marine microbial communities. In this Review, Peixoto and colleagues explore the effects of climate and anthropogenic stressors on microbiome composition and function across marine environments, assess their consequences for ecosystem functioning, and propose management and mitigation strategies to improve ocean health through a One Health perspective.

records.title: Predicting responses to prebiotic fibres: linking microbiota, function and clinical outcomes
records.description: Prebiotics and dietary fibre show highly individualized effects on gut microbiota and clinical outcomes, challenging their consistent effectiveness across populations. This Review examines the drivers of this variability, presents predictive approaches and discusses strategies to optimize prebiotic responses across individuals.

records.title: Author Correction: Phage therapy: from basic biology to clinical application
Aridity shifts plant–microorganism relationships
records.description: In this study, Wang et al. report that climate change-driven aridification shapes soil properties and plant–microorganism relationships across arid and semi-arid grasslands in China.

records.title: Urea reshuffles soil microbial balance
records.description: In this study, Wu and colleagues demonstrate that long-term nitrogen fertilization acidifies soils, altering soil properties and bacterial community composition in Tibetan alpine grasslands.

records.title: Growing forests to support soil health
records.description: This study provides evidence that afforestation and reforestation can increase soil carbon storage and support soil microbial communities, thus highlighting their potential in nature-based climate solutions.

records.title: Mosquito-based malaria control through genetic, microbial and immunological innovations
records.description: In this Review, Dong and colleagues overview recent developments in mosquito-targeted malaria control, highlighting Anopheles population modification (rendering mosquitoes Plasmodium -resistant) and Anopheles population-suppression strategies based on gene drive technology, engineered microorganisms, vaccines and drugs, and discuss key knowledge gaps and the responsible implementation of these approaches in conjunction with existing malaria interventions.

records.title: The role of the respiratory microbiome in acute and chronic respiratory diseases
records.description: In this Review, Heinzinger, Segal and Dickson summarize recent advances in our understanding of the respiratory microbiome in health, examine how it is altered in acute and chronic respiratory diseases, and discuss its diagnostic and therapeutic potential.

records.title: Remediation restores soil carbon
records.description: This study suggests that shifts in bioavailable heavy metals during soil remediation reshape microbial physiological traits, thereby increasing microbial carbon use efficiency and enhancing soil carbon storage.

records.title: Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses
records.description: In this Review, Neyts and colleagues discuss the rationale for developing broader-spectrum antivirals against RNA viruses, survey promising antiviral targets and agents, and outline strategies to accelerate clinical development and strengthen outbreak preparedness.

records.title: Predicting resistance evolution to guide antibiotic development
records.description: Resistance emergence is a major challenge to antibiotic development, often undermining promising drug candidates and negating years of research and pharmaceutical investment. In this Review, Pál and colleagues propose a resistance-based classification system for antibiotic development that integrates early resistance predictions into the prospective development of new antibiotics.

records.title: Cities cannot go green without soil microorganisms
records.description: Urban soils must move from providing single, engineered functions to supporting multifunctionality. Managing their microbiomes could simultaneously strengthen climate regulation, water retention, pollutant removal, biodiversity and human health, but only if biological restoration is coupled to risk assessment, long-term monitoring and equitable access.

records.title: How bacterial immune systems sense phage infection
records.description: Bacteria deploy diverse immune systems to counter phage infection, yet how these systems sense invasion remains incompletely understood. This Review categorizes phage-derived triggers and outlines emerging principles that govern immune recognition of phage infection.

records.title: Microbial ecology of shallow groundwater ecosystems
records.description: In this Review, Karwautz and Griebler examine the microbial communities found in shallow groundwater and aquifers, exploring their diversity, functional roles and dynamic interactions with adjacent terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, as well as the influence of global change and anthropogenic pressures on these microorganisms.

records.title: Rethinking soil microbiome interventions through an ecological lens
records.description: Microbial interventions offer sustainable opportunities to enhance soil health and ecosystem functioning, but they can also have unintended ecological consequences. This Comment explores their benefits and risks, arguing for a shift in perspective from microbial products as agricultural inputs to tools for ecological restoration.

records.title: Bifidobacteria: biogeography, host adaptation and ecological functions
records.description: In this Review, van Sinderen and colleagues explore how bifidobacteria evolved as an important human gut symbiont, highlighting genomic adaptations, metabolic versatility, ecological interactions and host-modulatory functions.

records.title: A four-way interaction in the rhizosphere
records.description: This Genome Watch discusses recent evidence on the interactions among a plant, a fungal pathogen, its bacterial endosymbiont and the rhizosphere microbiome, highlighting how such multipartite relationships shape plant health and disease, with implications for crop productivity in an era of global change.

records.title: After the rain in biocrusts
records.description: This study shows that rewetting activates a small, distinct subset of dryland biocrust bacteria, with mature communities showing greater microbial activity independent of light conditions.

records.title: Microsporidia: evolution, infection mechanisms and host impact
records.description: In this Review, Reinke examines recent advances in microsporidia research, from their evolution, to host invasion, proliferation, transmission, host interaction, immune evasion, detection and treatment, with a focus on species that infect humans, agriculturally important hosts and model systems.

records.title: Clostridioides difficile rewires the infant gut
records.description: In this study, Semon and colleagues examine the role of Clostridioides difficile colonization in early life and its lasting effects on host development.

records.title: Printing microbial partners for wastewater treatment
records.description: In this study, Liu and colleagues constructed engineered living materials to facilitate cross-feeding between anammox and dinitrifier species for efficient nitrate removal.

records.title: Publisher Correction: The HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein: structure, function and interactions with neutralizing antibodies
ND in Micro: neuroinclusion and neuroaffirmation for neurodivergent microbiologists
records.description: There is a growing awareness and visibility of neurodivergent people and our needs, but we still face workplace challenges. ND in Micro is a new global network that aims to connect, peer-support and raise the profile of neurodivergent microbiologists and our science through virtual and in-person activities and resources.

records.title: Prioritizing soil microbiome management and microbial restoration in low-income settings
records.description: Microbiome-based approaches can support climate-smart agriculture by promoting regenerative farming, eco-friendly land restoration and emissions reduction. In low-income settings, which are disproportionately affected by agricultural land degradation, these strategies can improve nutrient efficiency and reduce reliance on chemical inputs.

records.title: Separating microbial signal from noise
records.description: This Genome Watch explores how contamination and methodological assumptions influence the detection of tumour-associated microorganisms, highlighting the need for prospective, contamination-aware sequencing to distinguish biological signal from technical noise.

records.title: Colibactin defends honeybees
records.description: This study reports that colibactin production can protect honeybees against invading pathogenic bacteria, whereas co-evolved resident symbionts are protected by a resistance gene that allows them to coexist with the colibactin-producing bacteria.

records.title: Fungal Starship transposons for interspecies gene transfer
records.description: This Genome Watch article highlights how giant fungal Starship transposons may facilitate the horizontal transfer of smaller transposable elements and adaptive genes across species, contributing to rapid genome evolution and phenotypic diversification.

records.title: The gut microbiota in malnutrition
records.description: In this Review, Littlejohn et al. discuss the gut microbiota as a central contributor to malnutrition, including undernutrition, overnutrition, the double burden, and disease-related malnutrition. They synthesize evidence linking alterations in the gut microbiota to impaired nutrient utilization, inflammation and altered energy balance and discuss microbiota-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for improving outcomes across diverse populations and settings.

records.title: Phage therapy: from basic biology to clinical application
records.description: In this Review, Iredell and colleagues examine key aspects of phage biology and their relevance to phage therapy, and outline current approaches for clinical application of phages, along with their associated challenges.

records.title: Metabolic strategies of Enterobacteriaceae gut colonization
records.description: In this Review, Schubert and Hardt explore the metabolic strategies that Enterobacteriaceae use to establish themselves in the gut, and how they adapt to inflammatory conditions in this environment.

records.title: Chitin drives Candida auris skin persistence
records.description: This study shows that that Candida auris displays chitin on the surface that alters skin immune responses to promote persistent colonization.

records.title: Bacterial small regulatory RNAs
records.description: In this Review, Papenfort discusses established and emerging aspects of bacterial small RNAs (sRNAs), their molecular mechanisms and regulatory principles, and the global impact of sRNAs on cellular gene expression profiles.

records.title: Bacterial lipid structural diversity mediates commensalism and pathogenesis
records.description: In this Review, Heaver and Ley overview the different lipid structures present in commensal and pathogenic bacteria and their recognition by Toll-like receptor 2, Toll-like receptor 4 and CD1 molecules, highlighting the different effects on host immune responses.

records.title: Soil microbial conservation cannot rely on above-ground biodiversity
records.description: Soil biodiversity underpins ecosystem functioning and plant health, yet the incredible diversity of below-ground microorganisms remains largely overlooked in conservation efforts. This Comment outlines four key challenges to soil microbial conservation and emphasizes the importance of addressing them to safeguard soil biodiversity.

records.title: Infectious diseases in a changing climate
records.description: This Focus issue explores the links between climate change and infectious diseases and highlights the need for integrated, climate-informed responses. More broadly, this topic highlights the inequalities associated with the dual challenge posed by infectious diseases and climate change, with the greatest burdens falling on vulnerable populations.

records.title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis outpaces antibiotic treatment
records.description: This study reports that fast-growing intracellular Mycobacterium tuberculosis evades antibiotic treatment.

records.title: More resources, less microbial diversity
records.description: In a recent study, Shalev and colleagues demonstrate that enhanced resource diversity in microbial communities can reduce microbial biodiversity, challenging current ecological theories.

records.title: Within-host gene transfer drives tobramycin resistance
records.description: In a recent study, Karash and colleagues provide evidence for a resistance mechanism in which plasmid-mediated antibiotic resistance genes are horizontally transferred from transiently infecting bacteria to antibiotic-sensitive pathogens residing in patients’ lungs.

records.title: Impacts of pollution on the soil microbiome
records.description: In this Review, Zhu and colleagues overview the major types of soil pollution in the Anthropocene and their effects on soil microbiome composition, function and dynamics, while also exploring microbiome-based strategies to manage and mitigate soil pollution and safeguard environmental, plant, animal and human health.

records.title: Eggerthella lenta : metabolism, pathogenesis and therapeutic implications
records.description: Advancing microbiome research beyond well-studied bacterial species is key to understanding the full functional diversity and potential of the human gut microbiome. In this Review, Turnbaugh and colleagues explore the unique metabolism and pathogenic potential of Eggerthella lenta , supporting the feasibility and utility of studying diverse human-associated bacterial species.

records.title: Host–microbiota–pathogen interactions drive Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium pathogenesis
records.description: In this Review, Vázquez-Torres discusses our current understanding of how the dynamic interplay between microbial competition, host defences and Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium countermeasures determines the outcome of infection.

records.title: Echoes in the earth: how microbiomes help plants remember and resist
records.description: In this Genome Watch, we explore how the ecological memory of microbiomes shapes transgenerational stress resilience in plants.

records.title: Immune safeguarding as a conserved principle of antiviral defence
records.description: All organisms defend against viral infections through active immunity mechanisms that clear the virus or population-level mechanisms that cause regulated cell death. Recent research increasingly shows that, across all domains of life, these two types of defence systems are coupled such that regulated cell death mechanisms safeguard or back up active immunity.

records.title: Early microbial encounters, lasting effects: strains matter
records.description: This Genome Watch highlights recent evidence linking early-life gut microbial colonization to health benefits and cancer risk, shaped by strain-level microbial variation.

records.title: Emergence of human pathogenic fungi in a changing climate
records.description: As climate variability intensifies, human-pathogenic fungi are spreading into new regions and causing more disease. Addressing emergence will require stronger surveillance and forecasting; research on fungal dispersal, adaptation and population immunity; and policies that support vaccine development, antifungal stewardship and diagnostic access.

records.title: Waterborne diseases and climate change
records.description: In this Review, Levy and colleagues explore the relationships between climate change and waterborne diseases, discussing how the meteorological conditions that are influenced by climate change, including temperature, heavy rainfall and flooding, drought and extreme weather, affect the biology and transmission of waterborne pathogens, with a focus on those that spread via the faecal–oral route.

records.title: Climate change boosts Salmonella antimicrobial resistance
records.description: In this study, Zhou, Teng, Geng and colleagues report that warming and changes in precipitation patterns were associated with increased abundance of Salmonella antimicrobial resistance genes.

records.title: Climate factors and evolution drive cholera surges in Dhaka
records.description: This study suggests that both genomic evolution and climate factors shape the dynamics of cholera transmission and drive case surges in Dhaka city, Bangladesh.

records.title: Climate adaptation and biodiversity shape West Nile virus risk in cities
records.description: The study suggests that climate adaptation measures that increase urban biodiversity and green infrastructure may help to reduce local West Nile virus transmission in cities.

records.title: Bacterial vesicles protect the membrane during polymyxin stress
records.description: In this study, Bos and colleagues report previously uncharacterized roles for bacterial extracellular vesicles in membrane repair and tolerance to membrane-active antibiotics such as polymyxin B.

records.title: Reframing risk assessment for malaria elimination in a changing climate
records.description: Current malaria risk stratification approaches that support the global malaria eradication agenda are limited in capturing rapidly shifting pathogen transmission dynamics, unprecedented climate variability, extreme weather events, land use changes and population mobility. Omumbo, Hassell and Siwo propose reframing malaria burden-based metrics into anticipatory risk intelligence systems that leverage artificial intelligence tools.

records.title: Fermented food microbiome: influence on oral and gut microbiota, and human health
records.description: The bioactive compounds and microbial consortia contained in plant-based fermented foods support oral and gut microbiota, host immune function and metabolic resilience. This Review describes the impact of the fermented food microbiome on the oral–gut axis and identifies a strategic roadmap to integrate this edible microbiome into precision nutrition practices to promote health.

records.title: Coupling experiments and macroecological models to resolve multi-stressor effects in vector–pathogen systems
records.description: Mosquitoes, ticks and other vectors of infectious diseases are affected by interacting macroecological changes — climate change, biodiversity loss and environmental pollution — with multifaceted implications for human and animal health worldwide. We emphasize the need to establish the underlying mechanisms and anticipate future disease dynamics by integrating experiments, field observations and mechanistic, scenario-based modelling.

records.title: Klebsiella genus as driver of human disease: from infections to non-communicable disorders
records.description: Klebsiella spp. are mainly known as harmful, potentially drug-resistant, infectious agents, but they can also contribute to non-infectious diseases. In this Review, Porcari and colleagues discuss the pathogenic contribution of Klebsiella spp. to non-communicable disorders and the therapeutic strategies to treat and control the spread of these pathogens.

records.title: A new antibiotic scaffold hits a new target
records.description: This study describes the discovery of a new antibiotic with a previously unknown mode of action.

records.title: Bundibugyo virus outbreak: when a concerning pathogen meets a humanitarian emergency
records.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has declared its seventeenth Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, which had been circulating undetected for months. The response is now catching up across a region weakened by conflict, displacement and loss of humanitarian aid. With no licensed vaccine or treatment, containment will depend on rebuilding resources, access and trust in public health systems.

records.title: It takes three to modulate colitis
records.description: In this study, Zhou et. al identify a tripartite multi-kingdom microbial metabolic interaction network in the gut and its implications for inflammatory bowel disease.

records.title: Antimicrobial stewardship in LMICs: from paper promises to purpose-driven people
records.description: Antimicrobial stewardship in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) fails not for lack of policies but for lack of people. Sustainable progress depends on investing in mentored, purpose-driven local stewards who can adapt interventions to real-world constraints. Empowered multidisciplinary teams are a decisive force in slowing antimicrobial resistance where the burden is greatest.

records.title: A phage puts a new spin on bacterial flagella
records.description: This study reports that phage-mediated flagellin remodelling enhances bacterial motility, mammalian immune evasion and host colonization.

records.title: Impacts of climate change on dengue
records.description: Climate change, extreme weather and socioeconomic change drive surges in dengue and other mosquito-borne infectious diseases. Strengthening dengue resilience in a changing climate requires improved vector control, surveillance, climate-informed disease burden projections, sustainable urban and environmental management, and stronger community engagement. Partnerships that span health, environment, climate, economic and community sectors are critical for creating climate-resilient systems that improve health, environment and well-being.

records.title: Mechanisms of HIV-1 assembly, release and maturation
records.description: In this Review, Kleinpeter and Freed explore recent insights into HIV-1 assembly, release and maturation, showing how late-stage replication events prime infectivity. They also highlight progress in inhibitors targeting late-stage events and the therapeutic promise for people with HIV.

records.title: Infection cycles of viruses of the phylum Nucleocytoviricota
records.description: In this Review, Abergel et al. overview infection cycles across the Nucleocytoviricota phylum, highlighting shared mechanisms and lineage-specific features spanning viral entry, viral factory formation, genome replication, virion morphogenesis and egress, and discuss key unresolved questions in the field.

records.title: No escape for therapeutic bacteria
records.description: The results of this study advance the translation of implantable living materials towards clinical applications.

records.title: Agricultural intensification, microbial homogenization and loss of rare microbiota
records.description: In this Perspective, Banerjee, Dasgupta and van der Heijden discuss how intensive agricultural practices can lead to the taxonomic, physiological, genetic and functional homogenization of microbial communities and disproportionately affect rare microbiota.

records.title: An invasive plant reveals the importance of mycorrhizal fungi
records.description: In this Journal Club, Mark Anthony revisits a paper showing how an invasive plant disrupts mycorrhizal symbioses, reducing native tree seedling growth and reshaping forest communities.

records.title: Keeping off the weight with Akkermansia
records.description: In this study, Mount et al. conducted a randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial and identified pasteurized Akkermansia muciniphila Muc T as a potential strategy for weight loss maintenance.

records.title: Fungal diversity, ecology and functions in soil ecosystems
records.description: In this Review, Rillig explores the diversity of fungi in the soil ecosystem, their ecological interactions and diverse ecological roles in terrestrial ecosystems as well as anthropogenic factors that affect soil fungi.

records.title: Prophylaxis reimagined: innovation where vaccines and antibiotics fall short
records.description: This study demonstrates the use of a vectored immunoprophylaxis strategy using adeno-associated virus as an alternative approach for sustained in vivo antibody production against Staphylococcus aureus α-toxin.

records.title: Revisiting the life cycle of temperate phages
records.description: The life cycle of temperate bacteriophages involves lytic or lysogenic cycles and has historically served as a model for studying genetic regulation. This Review provides an updated overview of these cycles and highlights their complexities, supporting a greater appreciation of the ecological roles of temperate phages.

records.title: Ciliate hydrogen organelles fuel rumen methanogenesis
records.description: In this study, Xie et al. elucidate the mechanism through which ciliate protozoa contribute to methane emissions in ruminants.

records.title: Concepts of RNA virus evolution for the design of better antiviral countermeasures
records.description: In this Review, Tran and Vignuzzi examine how molecular processes and evolutionary pressures shape RNA virus diversity and adaptation. They outline how genome structure, mutational pathways and viral interactions influence evolutionary outcomes, offering insights relevant to the design of better vaccines and antiviral strategies.

records.title: Streptomyces deploys an ancient toxin to feast on insects
records.description: This study identified an exotoxin that is produced by Streptomyces that specifically kills insects.

records.title: Predation in microbial communities: gradients of nutritive killing
records.description: In this Review, Vasse and Velicer explore the phylogenetic and functional diversity of predators of microorganisms, conceptualizing the forms of microbial predation along gradients, including gradients of evolutionary adaptedness for predation and privatization of prey-derived nutrients.

records.title: Next-generation probiotics: an outlook into current applications and future developments
records.description: In this Review, Kern, Tofield, Frame and Elinav discuss recent advances in the design of next-generation probiotics, from identification of candidates to therapeutic applications across diverse disease contexts, and highlight major challenges and the potential of artificial intelligence to develop effective, personalized probiotics with therapeutic functions.

records.title: Next-generation probiotics: an outlook into current applications and future developments
records.description: In this Review, Kern, Tofield, Frame and Elinav discuss recent advances in the design of next-generation probiotics, from identification of candidates to therapeutic applications across diverse disease contexts, and highlight major challenges and the potential of artificial intelligence to develop effective, personalized probiotics with therapeutic functions.

records.title: Vibrio cholerae defends its way to success
records.description: This Genome Watch discusses the discovery of defence systems in pandemic Vibrio cholerae and their contribution to its ecological and evolutionary success.

records.title: Microorganisms lock up carbon in soil
records.description: In this Journal Club, Ashish Malik discusses a paper showing that soil microorganisms build stable soil organic matter.

records.title: In search of phage tail-like particles: nature’s versatile nanomachines
records.description: This Genome Watch article highlights the importance of predictive models for identifying and characterizing the roles of phage tail-like particles as a tool for bioengineering and biocontrol.

records.title: Present and future distribution of human pathogens in global soils
Shared signals shape phages’ lifestyles
records.description: Two back-to-back studies by Gallego-del-Sol et al. and Manley et al. demonstrate that arbitrium systems present in bacteriophages engage in cross-communication and modulate lysis–lysogeny decisions, with ecological implications.

records.title: Restoring soil and sediment microbiomes in the Anthropocene
records.description: In this Review, Wood and colleagues discuss how anthropogenic pressures are degrading soil and sediment microbiomes, propose restoration strategies and emphasize the importance of integrating microbiome science into global ecosystem restoration efforts.

records.title: Disentangling metabolic interactions within bacterial communities
Phage host range: determinants, dynamics and applications
records.description: Comprehensive assessment of the host range of phages is a prerequisite for their safe and effective use in multiple applications but is rarely undertaken. This Review outlines the molecular and ecological determinants of phage host range and discusses the importance of these determinants for developing phage-based applications.

records.title: Gut microorganisms in the middle of drug–drug interactions
records.description: This study highlights the role of the gut microbiome in shaping drug–drug interactions, with implications for treatment efficiency and patient outcome.

records.title: Mpox emergence, epidemiology, biology, clinical features and control
records.description: In this Review, Ogoina et al. examine the emergence of mpox and its epidemiology, the viral life cycle, transmission dynamics, risk factors and clinical characteristics. They also explore current and future prevention and control strategies, including the therapeutic and vaccine landscape, as well as the urgent need for integrated surveillance, equitable access to countermeasures, and Africa-led research to address the ongoing multi-clade threat.

records.title: The aquatic plastisphere: ecology, pathogen dissemination and antimicrobial resistance
records.description: In this Review, Ormsby and Quilliam discuss how plastic pollutants create a critical, novel habitat for complex microbial communities, highlighting the community composition, assembly dynamics and key functional traits of the plastisphere. They explore the dual public health risks of pathogen dissemination and enrichment of antimicrobial-resistance determinants.

records.title: Leveraging microbial phylogeny for computational efficiency
records.description: This Genome Watch article explores how taking into account known phylogenetic relationships can improve computational efficiency for genomics, enabling improved genome data compression and faster sequence search as datasets continue to expand.

records.title: Candida albicans steals magnesium and Pseudomonas aeruginosa unleashes resistance
records.description: This study uncovers how Pseudomonas aeruginosa acquires colistin resistance in magnesium-depleted environments created by Candida albicans by accumulating unique mutations in the lipid A biosynthetic pathway.

records.title: Microbial phosphorus cycling in terrestrial ecosystems
records.description: In this Review, the authors describe current knowledge of microbial phosphorus cycling in terrestrial ecosystems and discuss how microbial communities respond to environmental and anthropogenic pressures. They also propose the Microbial Phosphorus Adaptive Evolution Theory (MPAET) — a mechanistic framework linking persistent phosphorus limitation to evolutionary adaptations across cellular, genomic and community scales.

records.title: A trapped polymerase hastens avian influenza virus evolution
records.description: Funk and colleagues show that acquisition of a multibasic cleavage site in H5 haemagglutinin is the result of the combination of insertion-prone RNA sequences and the formation of transient RNA structures during replication by the viral RNA polymerase.

records.title: Bacterial allies against food anaphylaxis
records.description: This study shows that some human microbiota bacteria can metabolize immunodominant peanut allergens, thus modulating IgE-mediated anaphylaxis.

records.title: Human herpesvirus evasion of humoral immunity and implications for vaccine development
records.description: In this Review, Otero et al. explore how human herpesviruses evade humoral immune responses and consider the resulting implications for developing effective vaccines and treatments for diseases caused by these common viral pathogens.

records.title: Reverse vaccinology 3.0
records.description: Andreano, McLellan and Rappuoli introduce ‘reverse vaccinology 3.0’, a transformative approach that could revolutionize the field of vaccinology and contribute to addressing global health challenges.

records.title: Impacts of climate extremes on plant pathogens, microbiomes and plant health
records.description: In this Review, Singh and colleagues discuss the impacts of key climate extremes on soil-borne pathogens, plant microbiomes and host physiology that ultimately determine disease outcomes, as well as the eco-evolutionary mechanisms by which pathogens, hosts and microbiomes may adapt to climate extremes. Finally, they propose an integrated pathway for harnessing microbiomes to address the critical challenges posed by climate extremes.

records.title: Bordetella hides in the cilia forest
records.description: This study shows that FhaB is a critical colonization factor that enables Bordetella species to colonize a protected niche at the base of the cilia of epithelial cells.

records.title: Diversity, ecology, cell biology and evolution of the Asgard archaea
records.description: The Asgard archaea have become a cornerstone of archaeal research, particularly for studies aiming to unravel the origin and early evolution of eukaryotes. This Review outlines the current state of the research field focusing on these intriguing microorganisms and discusses future research directions aiming to resolve their diversity, ecology, cell biology and evolution.

records.title: Publisher Correction: Tick-borne viruses: discovery, clinical aspects, influencing factors and control
Iron acquisition by amino acids under flow
records.description: This study shows that amino acids facilitate microbial iron acquisition in environments that exhibit low nutrient concentration and where siderophores are highly diluted.

records.title: Probing the host cell exit strategy of Babesia divergens
records.description: This study uncovers druggable kinases and proteases required for host cell egress of the apicomplexan parasite Babesia divergens .

records.title: Varicella zoster virus and the central nervous system
records.description: Varicella zoster virus (VZV) infection causes varicella and herpes zoster and, rarely, severe central nervous system (CNS) complications, including encephalitis. Ogunjimi et al. review the evidence linking herpes zoster with stroke and dementia, summarize innate and adaptive immune responses to VZV-related CNS disease, and debate the consequences of vaccination.

records.title: Gut microbiome control of HIV immunodeficiency
records.description: A recent study found that HIV-associated changes in the gut microbiome correlate with peripheral CD4 + T cell counts and are linked to differences in mucosal immune responses and susceptibility to opportunistic infection.

records.title: How flaviviruses choose their mosquito
records.description: This study identified the molecular mechanisms that contribute to species specificity and compatibility between mosquito vectors and flavivirus species.

records.title: Predicting phage–host specificity
records.description: This Genome Watch article explores how protein language models are transforming phage–host specificity prediction by capturing meaningful biological information from viral sequences, from individual proteins to entire genomes.

records.title: Climate change and antimicrobial resistance
records.description: In this work, Kalanxhi and Laxminarayan review the evidence supporting the links between climate change and antimicrobial resistance, highlight opportunities for action and identify areas wherein further research is needed to understand the nature of these complex relationships.

records.title: The paradox of immune systems conservation between prokaryotes and eukaryotes
records.description: The widespread prokaryotic immune systems, in particular restriction–modification, CRISPR–Cas and defensive toxin–antitoxin systems, are absent in eukaryotes, whereas relatively rare ones, such as Argonautes and antiviral STAND NTPases, became central to eukaryotic innate immunity. In this Comment, we hypothesize that the cause of this paradox is the drastic reduction of horizontal gene transfer rate in eukaryotes.

records.title: Oral–gut bacterial transport drives chronic liver disease
records.description: A study by Jin et al. shows that oral–gut translocation of prtC + bacteria is implicated in the well-known link between gut microbiome dysbiosis and advanced liver disease in humans.

records.title: Phage–host dynamics in space
records.description: This study shows that microgravity modulates phage–host co-evolution and alters their mutational landscapes, facilitating adaptation to such a distinct environmental niche.

records.title: Tree bark microbiota in climate-active gas cycling
records.description: This study reports that the tree bark microbial community actively modulates fluxes of climate-active gases and volatile organic compounds, and may mediate global atmospheric gas cycling.

records.title: Flipping the drug resistance switch
records.description: A recent study identifies a compound that sensitizes fungal pathogens to the antifungal drug caspofungin.

records.title: Panning for gold: incidentally sequenced DNA
records.description: This Genome Watch explores how large-scale reference genome initiatives offer an unparalleled opportunity to generate sequencing data from under-represented cobionts (organisms sequenced alongside target organisms), including intracellular parasites.

records.title: Tick-borne viruses: discovery, clinical aspects, influencing factors and control
records.description: Pathogenic tick-borne viruses (TBVs) are a global threat to public and veterinary health. In this Review, Cao and colleagues highlight the diversity of the tick virome, review human and animal TBV pathogens, outline clinical features of human TBV infections, describe factors impacting ticks and TBV spread, and discuss the need for integrated One Health control strategies.

records.title: Chemical whispers hidden in the plant and microbiota kingdoms
records.description: In this Journal Club, Mengcen Wang discusses papers that uncover chemical crosstalk between plants and their microbiota.

records.title: The gut microbiome in solid-organ and haematopoietic-stem-cell transplantation
records.description: Swarte, Zhang and colleagues review the microbiome in solid-organ transplantation and allogeneic haematopoietic-stem-cell transplantation recipients, considering the effects of the intestinal environment, interactions between the microbiota and immunosuppressive drugs, and effects of dysbiosis on transplantation outcomes. The potential of microbiome-targeted interventions to improve transplantation outcomes is also discussed.

records.title: Harnessing the microbiome for cancer therapy
records.description: In this Review, Hajjar, Mars and Kashyap discuss the role of the microbiome in cancer development and progression and in treatment response. They also consider the potential of the microbiome as a therapeutic target and as a prognostic and predictive biomarker, and outline major knowledge gaps in the field.

records.title: Keystone concept revisited: insights into microbial community dynamics and control
records.description: In this Perspective, Garza et al. revisit the keystone concept and discuss its relevance for microbial keystone taxa and functions. For this, they explore the different mechanisms behind keystoneness, cover the strengths and weaknesses of current keystone prediction methods, present recent findings on keystone taxa and functions and explore the role of keystones in community control.

records.title: Uncovering a clostridial toxin behind necrotizing enterocolitis
records.description: In a recent study, Zhang and colleagues identify Delta toxin produced by Clostridium perfringens as the driver of intestinal and brain injury in a subset of necrotizing enterocolitis.

records.title: The soil microbiome in an era of global change
records.description: Soils and their microbiomes are being severely affected by rapid global change. Understanding the effects of anthropogenic stressors on the soil microbiome is therefore key to improving soil resilience and ensuring planetary health. This Focus issue highlights the pressing threats to belowground microbial biodiversity and the opportunities and challenges to restore it.

records.title: The small intestine microbiome: composition, host interactions and therapeutic potential
records.description: In this Review, Britton and colleagues examine the composition of the small intestinal microbiome and its interactions with the host, highlighting emerging insights into its roles in physiology and health. They also discuss the challenges of studying this understudied microbial community and its potential as a source of future microbial therapeutics.

records.title: The microbiome’s voyage beyond Earth
records.description: This Genome Watch discusses how spaceflights affect microbiome composition and dynamics, highlighting how integrating metabolic and host data with microbiome monitoring could support astronaut health during long-term deep-space missions.

records.title: The mammalian archaeome: diversity, function and emerging roles in health and disease
records.description: In this Review, Moissl-Eichinger and colleagues explore the distribution, diversity and function of the mammalian archaeome, with a focus on humans and ruminants. They explore the ecological and physiological roles of Methanobrevibacter spp. as key gastrointestinal colonizers, the archaeal interactions with bacterial communities and the host, and the impact of health and disease on the human archaeome.

records.title: The contextual pathogenicity of Porphyromonas gingivalis
records.description: In this Review, Lamont and Hajishengallis explore how the pathogenicity of Porphyromonas gingivalis is determined by microbial, metabolic and host context. They discuss how community interactions, nutrient-sensing and immune subversion regulate virulence and drive dysbiosis, inflammation and periodontitis progression.

records.title: Global change reshapes marine microbial communities, functions and One Health outcomes
records.description: Global change is transforming marine microbial communities. In this Review, Peixoto and colleagues explore the effects of climate and anthropogenic stressors on microbiome composition and function across marine environments, assess their consequences for ecosystem functioning, and propose management and mitigation strategies to improve ocean health through a One Health perspective.

records.title: Predicting responses to prebiotic fibres: linking microbiota, function and clinical outcomes
records.description: Prebiotics and dietary fibre show highly individualized effects on gut microbiota and clinical outcomes, challenging their consistent effectiveness across populations. This Review examines the drivers of this variability, presents predictive approaches and discusses strategies to optimize prebiotic responses across individuals.

records.title: Author Correction: Phage therapy: from basic biology to clinical application
Aridity shifts plant–microorganism relationships
records.description: In this study, Wang et al. report that climate change-driven aridification shapes soil properties and plant–microorganism relationships across arid and semi-arid grasslands in China.

records.title: Urea reshuffles soil microbial balance
records.description: In this study, Wu and colleagues demonstrate that long-term nitrogen fertilization acidifies soils, altering soil properties and bacterial community composition in Tibetan alpine grasslands.

records.title: Growing forests to support soil health
records.description: This study provides evidence that afforestation and reforestation can increase soil carbon storage and support soil microbial communities, thus highlighting their potential in nature-based climate solutions.

records.title: Mosquito-based malaria control through genetic, microbial and immunological innovations
records.description: In this Review, Dong and colleagues overview recent developments in mosquito-targeted malaria control, highlighting Anopheles population modification (rendering mosquitoes Plasmodium -resistant) and Anopheles population-suppression strategies based on gene drive technology, engineered microorganisms, vaccines and drugs, and discuss key knowledge gaps and the responsible implementation of these approaches in conjunction with existing malaria interventions.

records.title: The role of the respiratory microbiome in acute and chronic respiratory diseases
records.description: In this Review, Heinzinger, Segal and Dickson summarize recent advances in our understanding of the respiratory microbiome in health, examine how it is altered in acute and chronic respiratory diseases, and discuss its diagnostic and therapeutic potential.

records.title: Remediation restores soil carbon
records.description: This study suggests that shifts in bioavailable heavy metals during soil remediation reshape microbial physiological traits, thereby increasing microbial carbon use efficiency and enhancing soil carbon storage.

records.title: Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses
records.description: In this Review, Neyts and colleagues discuss the rationale for developing broader-spectrum antivirals against RNA viruses, survey promising antiviral targets and agents, and outline strategies to accelerate clinical development and strengthen outbreak preparedness.

records.title: Predicting resistance evolution to guide antibiotic development
records.description: Resistance emergence is a major challenge to antibiotic development, often undermining promising drug candidates and negating years of research and pharmaceutical investment. In this Review, Pál and colleagues propose a resistance-based classification system for antibiotic development that integrates early resistance predictions into the prospective development of new antibiotics.

records.title: Cities cannot go green without soil microorganisms
records.description: Urban soils must move from providing single, engineered functions to supporting multifunctionality. Managing their microbiomes could simultaneously strengthen climate regulation, water retention, pollutant removal, biodiversity and human health, but only if biological restoration is coupled to risk assessment, long-term monitoring and equitable access.

records.title: How bacterial immune systems sense phage infection
records.description: Bacteria deploy diverse immune systems to counter phage infection, yet how these systems sense invasion remains incompletely understood. This Review categorizes phage-derived triggers and outlines emerging principles that govern immune recognition of phage infection.

records.title: Microbial ecology of shallow groundwater ecosystems
records.description: In this Review, Karwautz and Griebler examine the microbial communities found in shallow groundwater and aquifers, exploring their diversity, functional roles and dynamic interactions with adjacent terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, as well as the influence of global change and anthropogenic pressures on these microorganisms.

records.title: Rethinking soil microbiome interventions through an ecological lens
records.description: Microbial interventions offer sustainable opportunities to enhance soil health and ecosystem functioning, but they can also have unintended ecological consequences. This Comment explores their benefits and risks, arguing for a shift in perspective from microbial products as agricultural inputs to tools for ecological restoration.

records.title: Bifidobacteria: biogeography, host adaptation and ecological functions
records.description: In this Review, van Sinderen and colleagues explore how bifidobacteria evolved as an important human gut symbiont, highlighting genomic adaptations, metabolic versatility, ecological interactions and host-modulatory functions.

records.title: A four-way interaction in the rhizosphere
records.description: This Genome Watch discusses recent evidence on the interactions among a plant, a fungal pathogen, its bacterial endosymbiont and the rhizosphere microbiome, highlighting how such multipartite relationships shape plant health and disease, with implications for crop productivity in an era of global change.

records.title: After the rain in biocrusts
records.description: This study shows that rewetting activates a small, distinct subset of dryland biocrust bacteria, with mature communities showing greater microbial activity independent of light conditions.

records.title: Microsporidia: evolution, infection mechanisms and host impact
records.description: In this Review, Reinke examines recent advances in microsporidia research, from their evolution, to host invasion, proliferation, transmission, host interaction, immune evasion, detection and treatment, with a focus on species that infect humans, agriculturally important hosts and model systems.

records.title: Clostridioides difficile rewires the infant gut
records.description: In this study, Semon and colleagues examine the role of Clostridioides difficile colonization in early life and its lasting effects on host development.

records.title: Printing microbial partners for wastewater treatment
records.description: In this study, Liu and colleagues constructed engineered living materials to facilitate cross-feeding between anammox and dinitrifier species for efficient nitrate removal.

records.title: Publisher Correction: The HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein: structure, function and interactions with neutralizing antibodies
ND in Micro: neuroinclusion and neuroaffirmation for neurodivergent microbiologists
records.description: There is a growing awareness and visibility of neurodivergent people and our needs, but we still face workplace challenges. ND in Micro is a new global network that aims to connect, peer-support and raise the profile of neurodivergent microbiologists and our science through virtual and in-person activities and resources.

records.title: Prioritizing soil microbiome management and microbial restoration in low-income settings
records.description: Microbiome-based approaches can support climate-smart agriculture by promoting regenerative farming, eco-friendly land restoration and emissions reduction. In low-income settings, which are disproportionately affected by agricultural land degradation, these strategies can improve nutrient efficiency and reduce reliance on chemical inputs.

records.title: Separating microbial signal from noise
records.description: This Genome Watch explores how contamination and methodological assumptions influence the detection of tumour-associated microorganisms, highlighting the need for prospective, contamination-aware sequencing to distinguish biological signal from technical noise.

records.title: Colibactin defends honeybees
records.description: This study reports that colibactin production can protect honeybees against invading pathogenic bacteria, whereas co-evolved resident symbionts are protected by a resistance gene that allows them to coexist with the colibactin-producing bacteria.

records.title: Fungal Starship transposons for interspecies gene transfer
records.description: This Genome Watch article highlights how giant fungal Starship transposons may facilitate the horizontal transfer of smaller transposable elements and adaptive genes across species, contributing to rapid genome evolution and phenotypic diversification.

records.title: The gut microbiota in malnutrition
records.description: In this Review, Littlejohn et al. discuss the gut microbiota as a central contributor to malnutrition, including undernutrition, overnutrition, the double burden, and disease-related malnutrition. They synthesize evidence linking alterations in the gut microbiota to impaired nutrient utilization, inflammation and altered energy balance and discuss microbiota-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for improving outcomes across diverse populations and settings.

records.title: Phage therapy: from basic biology to clinical application
records.description: In this Review, Iredell and colleagues examine key aspects of phage biology and their relevance to phage therapy, and outline current approaches for clinical application of phages, along with their associated challenges.

records.title: Metabolic strategies of Enterobacteriaceae gut colonization
records.description: In this Review, Schubert and Hardt explore the metabolic strategies that Enterobacteriaceae use to establish themselves in the gut, and how they adapt to inflammatory conditions in this environment.

records.title: Chitin drives Candida auris skin persistence
records.description: This study shows that that Candida auris displays chitin on the surface that alters skin immune responses to promote persistent colonization.

records.title: Bacterial small regulatory RNAs
records.description: In this Review, Papenfort discusses established and emerging aspects of bacterial small RNAs (sRNAs), their molecular mechanisms and regulatory principles, and the global impact of sRNAs on cellular gene expression profiles.

records.title: Bacterial lipid structural diversity mediates commensalism and pathogenesis
records.description: In this Review, Heaver and Ley overview the different lipid structures present in commensal and pathogenic bacteria and their recognition by Toll-like receptor 2, Toll-like receptor 4 and CD1 molecules, highlighting the different effects on host immune responses.

records.title: Soil microbial conservation cannot rely on above-ground biodiversity
records.description: Soil biodiversity underpins ecosystem functioning and plant health, yet the incredible diversity of below-ground microorganisms remains largely overlooked in conservation efforts. This Comment outlines four key challenges to soil microbial conservation and emphasizes the importance of addressing them to safeguard soil biodiversity.

records.title: Infectious diseases in a changing climate
records.description: This Focus issue explores the links between climate change and infectious diseases and highlights the need for integrated, climate-informed responses. More broadly, this topic highlights the inequalities associated with the dual challenge posed by infectious diseases and climate change, with the greatest burdens falling on vulnerable populations.

records.title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis outpaces antibiotic treatment
records.description: This study reports that fast-growing intracellular Mycobacterium tuberculosis evades antibiotic treatment.

records.title: More resources, less microbial diversity
records.description: In a recent study, Shalev and colleagues demonstrate that enhanced resource diversity in microbial communities can reduce microbial biodiversity, challenging current ecological theories.

records.title: Within-host gene transfer drives tobramycin resistance
records.description: In a recent study, Karash and colleagues provide evidence for a resistance mechanism in which plasmid-mediated antibiotic resistance genes are horizontally transferred from transiently infecting bacteria to antibiotic-sensitive pathogens residing in patients’ lungs.

records.title: Impacts of pollution on the soil microbiome
records.description: In this Review, Zhu and colleagues overview the major types of soil pollution in the Anthropocene and their effects on soil microbiome composition, function and dynamics, while also exploring microbiome-based strategies to manage and mitigate soil pollution and safeguard environmental, plant, animal and human health.

records.title: Eggerthella lenta : metabolism, pathogenesis and therapeutic implications
records.description: Advancing microbiome research beyond well-studied bacterial species is key to understanding the full functional diversity and potential of the human gut microbiome. In this Review, Turnbaugh and colleagues explore the unique metabolism and pathogenic potential of Eggerthella lenta , supporting the feasibility and utility of studying diverse human-associated bacterial species.

records.title: Host–microbiota–pathogen interactions drive Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium pathogenesis
records.description: In this Review, Vázquez-Torres discusses our current understanding of how the dynamic interplay between microbial competition, host defences and Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium countermeasures determines the outcome of infection.

records.title: Echoes in the earth: how microbiomes help plants remember and resist
records.description: In this Genome Watch, we explore how the ecological memory of microbiomes shapes transgenerational stress resilience in plants.

records.title: Immune safeguarding as a conserved principle of antiviral defence
records.description: All organisms defend against viral infections through active immunity mechanisms that clear the virus or population-level mechanisms that cause regulated cell death. Recent research increasingly shows that, across all domains of life, these two types of defence systems are coupled such that regulated cell death mechanisms safeguard or back up active immunity.

records.title: Early microbial encounters, lasting effects: strains matter
records.description: This Genome Watch highlights recent evidence linking early-life gut microbial colonization to health benefits and cancer risk, shaped by strain-level microbial variation.

records.title: Emergence of human pathogenic fungi in a changing climate
records.description: As climate variability intensifies, human-pathogenic fungi are spreading into new regions and causing more disease. Addressing emergence will require stronger surveillance and forecasting; research on fungal dispersal, adaptation and population immunity; and policies that support vaccine development, antifungal stewardship and diagnostic access.

records.title: Waterborne diseases and climate change
records.description: In this Review, Levy and colleagues explore the relationships between climate change and waterborne diseases, discussing how the meteorological conditions that are influenced by climate change, including temperature, heavy rainfall and flooding, drought and extreme weather, affect the biology and transmission of waterborne pathogens, with a focus on those that spread via the faecal–oral route.

records.title: Climate change boosts Salmonella antimicrobial resistance
records.description: In this study, Zhou, Teng, Geng and colleagues report that warming and changes in precipitation patterns were associated with increased abundance of Salmonella antimicrobial resistance genes.

records.title: Climate factors and evolution drive cholera surges in Dhaka
records.description: This study suggests that both genomic evolution and climate factors shape the dynamics of cholera transmission and drive case surges in Dhaka city, Bangladesh.

records.title: Climate adaptation and biodiversity shape West Nile virus risk in cities
records.description: The study suggests that climate adaptation measures that increase urban biodiversity and green infrastructure may help to reduce local West Nile virus transmission in cities.

records.title: Bacterial vesicles protect the membrane during polymyxin stress
records.description: In this study, Bos and colleagues report previously uncharacterized roles for bacterial extracellular vesicles in membrane repair and tolerance to membrane-active antibiotics such as polymyxin B.

records.title: Reframing risk assessment for malaria elimination in a changing climate
records.description: Current malaria risk stratification approaches that support the global malaria eradication agenda are limited in capturing rapidly shifting pathogen transmission dynamics, unprecedented climate variability, extreme weather events, land use changes and population mobility. Omumbo, Hassell and Siwo propose reframing malaria burden-based metrics into anticipatory risk intelligence systems that leverage artificial intelligence tools.

records.title: Fermented food microbiome: influence on oral and gut microbiota, and human health
records.description: The bioactive compounds and microbial consortia contained in plant-based fermented foods support oral and gut microbiota, host immune function and metabolic resilience. This Review describes the impact of the fermented food microbiome on the oral–gut axis and identifies a strategic roadmap to integrate this edible microbiome into precision nutrition practices to promote health.

records.title: Coupling experiments and macroecological models to resolve multi-stressor effects in vector–pathogen systems
records.description: Mosquitoes, ticks and other vectors of infectious diseases are affected by interacting macroecological changes — climate change, biodiversity loss and environmental pollution — with multifaceted implications for human and animal health worldwide. We emphasize the need to establish the underlying mechanisms and anticipate future disease dynamics by integrating experiments, field observations and mechanistic, scenario-based modelling.

records.title: Klebsiella genus as driver of human disease: from infections to non-communicable disorders
records.description: Klebsiella spp. are mainly known as harmful, potentially drug-resistant, infectious agents, but they can also contribute to non-infectious diseases. In this Review, Porcari and colleagues discuss the pathogenic contribution of Klebsiella spp. to non-communicable disorders and the therapeutic strategies to treat and control the spread of these pathogens.

records.title: A new antibiotic scaffold hits a new target
records.description: This study describes the discovery of a new antibiotic with a previously unknown mode of action.

records.title: Bundibugyo virus outbreak: when a concerning pathogen meets a humanitarian emergency
records.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has declared its seventeenth Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, which had been circulating undetected for months. The response is now catching up across a region weakened by conflict, displacement and loss of humanitarian aid. With no licensed vaccine or treatment, containment will depend on rebuilding resources, access and trust in public health systems.

records.title: It takes three to modulate colitis
records.description: In this study, Zhou et. al identify a tripartite multi-kingdom microbial metabolic interaction network in the gut and its implications for inflammatory bowel disease.

records.title: Antimicrobial stewardship in LMICs: from paper promises to purpose-driven people
records.description: Antimicrobial stewardship in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) fails not for lack of policies but for lack of people. Sustainable progress depends on investing in mentored, purpose-driven local stewards who can adapt interventions to real-world constraints. Empowered multidisciplinary teams are a decisive force in slowing antimicrobial resistance where the burden is greatest.

records.title: A phage puts a new spin on bacterial flagella
records.description: This study reports that phage-mediated flagellin remodelling enhances bacterial motility, mammalian immune evasion and host colonization.

records.title: Impacts of climate change on dengue
records.description: Climate change, extreme weather and socioeconomic change drive surges in dengue and other mosquito-borne infectious diseases. Strengthening dengue resilience in a changing climate requires improved vector control, surveillance, climate-informed disease burden projections, sustainable urban and environmental management, and stronger community engagement. Partnerships that span health, environment, climate, economic and community sectors are critical for creating climate-resilient systems that improve health, environment and well-being.

records.title: Mechanisms of HIV-1 assembly, release and maturation
records.description: In this Review, Kleinpeter and Freed explore recent insights into HIV-1 assembly, release and maturation, showing how late-stage replication events prime infectivity. They also highlight progress in inhibitors targeting late-stage events and the therapeutic promise for people with HIV.

records.title: Infection cycles of viruses of the phylum Nucleocytoviricota
records.description: In this Review, Abergel et al. overview infection cycles across the Nucleocytoviricota phylum, highlighting shared mechanisms and lineage-specific features spanning viral entry, viral factory formation, genome replication, virion morphogenesis and egress, and discuss key unresolved questions in the field.

records.title: No escape for therapeutic bacteria
records.description: The results of this study advance the translation of implantable living materials towards clinical applications.

records.title: Agricultural intensification, microbial homogenization and loss of rare microbiota
records.description: In this Perspective, Banerjee, Dasgupta and van der Heijden discuss how intensive agricultural practices can lead to the taxonomic, physiological, genetic and functional homogenization of microbial communities and disproportionately affect rare microbiota.

records.title: An invasive plant reveals the importance of mycorrhizal fungi
records.description: In this Journal Club, Mark Anthony revisits a paper showing how an invasive plant disrupts mycorrhizal symbioses, reducing native tree seedling growth and reshaping forest communities.

records.title: Keeping off the weight with Akkermansia
records.description: In this study, Mount et al. conducted a randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial and identified pasteurized Akkermansia muciniphila Muc T as a potential strategy for weight loss maintenance.

records.title: Fungal diversity, ecology and functions in soil ecosystems
records.description: In this Review, Rillig explores the diversity of fungi in the soil ecosystem, their ecological interactions and diverse ecological roles in terrestrial ecosystems as well as anthropogenic factors that affect soil fungi.

records.title: Prophylaxis reimagined: innovation where vaccines and antibiotics fall short
records.description: This study demonstrates the use of a vectored immunoprophylaxis strategy using adeno-associated virus as an alternative approach for sustained in vivo antibody production against Staphylococcus aureus α-toxin.

records.title: Revisiting the life cycle of temperate phages
records.description: The life cycle of temperate bacteriophages involves lytic or lysogenic cycles and has historically served as a model for studying genetic regulation. This Review provides an updated overview of these cycles and highlights their complexities, supporting a greater appreciation of the ecological roles of temperate phages.

records.title: Ciliate hydrogen organelles fuel rumen methanogenesis
records.description: In this study, Xie et al. elucidate the mechanism through which ciliate protozoa contribute to methane emissions in ruminants.

records.title: Concepts of RNA virus evolution for the design of better antiviral countermeasures
records.description: In this Review, Tran and Vignuzzi examine how molecular processes and evolutionary pressures shape RNA virus diversity and adaptation. They outline how genome structure, mutational pathways and viral interactions influence evolutionary outcomes, offering insights relevant to the design of better vaccines and antiviral strategies.

records.title: Streptomyces deploys an ancient toxin to feast on insects
records.description: This study identified an exotoxin that is produced by Streptomyces that specifically kills insects.

records.title: Predation in microbial communities: gradients of nutritive killing
records.description: In this Review, Vasse and Velicer explore the phylogenetic and functional diversity of predators of microorganisms, conceptualizing the forms of microbial predation along gradients, including gradients of evolutionary adaptedness for predation and privatization of prey-derived nutrients.

records.title: Next-generation probiotics: an outlook into current applications and future developments
records.description: In this Review, Kern, Tofield, Frame and Elinav discuss recent advances in the design of next-generation probiotics, from identification of candidates to therapeutic applications across diverse disease contexts, and highlight major challenges and the potential of artificial intelligence to develop effective, personalized probiotics with therapeutic functions.

records.title: Next-generation probiotics: an outlook into current applications and future developments
records.description: In this Review, Kern, Tofield, Frame and Elinav discuss recent advances in the design of next-generation probiotics, from identification of candidates to therapeutic applications across diverse disease contexts, and highlight major challenges and the potential of artificial intelligence to develop effective, personalized probiotics with therapeutic functions.

records.title: Vibrio cholerae defends its way to success
records.description: This Genome Watch discusses the discovery of defence systems in pandemic Vibrio cholerae and their contribution to its ecological and evolutionary success.

records.title: Microorganisms lock up carbon in soil
records.description: In this Journal Club, Ashish Malik discusses a paper showing that soil microorganisms build stable soil organic matter.

records.title: In search of phage tail-like particles: nature’s versatile nanomachines
records.description: This Genome Watch article highlights the importance of predictive models for identifying and characterizing the roles of phage tail-like particles as a tool for bioengineering and biocontrol.

records.title: Present and future distribution of human pathogens in global soils
Shared signals shape phages’ lifestyles
records.description: Two back-to-back studies by Gallego-del-Sol et al. and Manley et al. demonstrate that arbitrium systems present in bacteriophages engage in cross-communication and modulate lysis–lysogeny decisions, with ecological implications.

records.title: Restoring soil and sediment microbiomes in the Anthropocene
records.description: In this Review, Wood and colleagues discuss how anthropogenic pressures are degrading soil and sediment microbiomes, propose restoration strategies and emphasize the importance of integrating microbiome science into global ecosystem restoration efforts.

records.title: Disentangling metabolic interactions within bacterial communities
Phage host range: determinants, dynamics and applications
records.description: Comprehensive assessment of the host range of phages is a prerequisite for their safe and effective use in multiple applications but is rarely undertaken. This Review outlines the molecular and ecological determinants of phage host range and discusses the importance of these determinants for developing phage-based applications.

records.title: Gut microorganisms in the middle of drug–drug interactions
records.description: This study highlights the role of the gut microbiome in shaping drug–drug interactions, with implications for treatment efficiency and patient outcome.

records.title: Mpox emergence, epidemiology, biology, clinical features and control
records.description: In this Review, Ogoina et al. examine the emergence of mpox and its epidemiology, the viral life cycle, transmission dynamics, risk factors and clinical characteristics. They also explore current and future prevention and control strategies, including the therapeutic and vaccine landscape, as well as the urgent need for integrated surveillance, equitable access to countermeasures, and Africa-led research to address the ongoing multi-clade threat.

records.title: The aquatic plastisphere: ecology, pathogen dissemination and antimicrobial resistance
records.description: In this Review, Ormsby and Quilliam discuss how plastic pollutants create a critical, novel habitat for complex microbial communities, highlighting the community composition, assembly dynamics and key functional traits of the plastisphere. They explore the dual public health risks of pathogen dissemination and enrichment of antimicrobial-resistance determinants.

records.title: Leveraging microbial phylogeny for computational efficiency
records.description: This Genome Watch article explores how taking into account known phylogenetic relationships can improve computational efficiency for genomics, enabling improved genome data compression and faster sequence search as datasets continue to expand.

records.title: Candida albicans steals magnesium and Pseudomonas aeruginosa unleashes resistance
records.description: This study uncovers how Pseudomonas aeruginosa acquires colistin resistance in magnesium-depleted environments created by Candida albicans by accumulating unique mutations in the lipid A biosynthetic pathway.

records.title: Microbial phosphorus cycling in terrestrial ecosystems
records.description: In this Review, the authors describe current knowledge of microbial phosphorus cycling in terrestrial ecosystems and discuss how microbial communities respond to environmental and anthropogenic pressures. They also propose the Microbial Phosphorus Adaptive Evolution Theory (MPAET) — a mechanistic framework linking persistent phosphorus limitation to evolutionary adaptations across cellular, genomic and community scales.

records.title: A trapped polymerase hastens avian influenza virus evolution
records.description: Funk and colleagues show that acquisition of a multibasic cleavage site in H5 haemagglutinin is the result of the combination of insertion-prone RNA sequences and the formation of transient RNA structures during replication by the viral RNA polymerase.

records.title: Bacterial allies against food anaphylaxis
records.description: This study shows that some human microbiota bacteria can metabolize immunodominant peanut allergens, thus modulating IgE-mediated anaphylaxis.

records.title: Human herpesvirus evasion of humoral immunity and implications for vaccine development
records.description: In this Review, Otero et al. explore how human herpesviruses evade humoral immune responses and consider the resulting implications for developing effective vaccines and treatments for diseases caused by these common viral pathogens.

records.title: Reverse vaccinology 3.0
records.description: Andreano, McLellan and Rappuoli introduce ‘reverse vaccinology 3.0’, a transformative approach that could revolutionize the field of vaccinology and contribute to addressing global health challenges.

records.title: Impacts of climate extremes on plant pathogens, microbiomes and plant health
records.description: In this Review, Singh and colleagues discuss the impacts of key climate extremes on soil-borne pathogens, plant microbiomes and host physiology that ultimately determine disease outcomes, as well as the eco-evolutionary mechanisms by which pathogens, hosts and microbiomes may adapt to climate extremes. Finally, they propose an integrated pathway for harnessing microbiomes to address the critical challenges posed by climate extremes.

records.title: Bordetella hides in the cilia forest
records.description: This study shows that FhaB is a critical colonization factor that enables Bordetella species to colonize a protected niche at the base of the cilia of epithelial cells.

records.title: Diversity, ecology, cell biology and evolution of the Asgard archaea
records.description: The Asgard archaea have become a cornerstone of archaeal research, particularly for studies aiming to unravel the origin and early evolution of eukaryotes. This Review outlines the current state of the research field focusing on these intriguing microorganisms and discusses future research directions aiming to resolve their diversity, ecology, cell biology and evolution.

records.title: Publisher Correction: Tick-borne viruses: discovery, clinical aspects, influencing factors and control
Iron acquisition by amino acids under flow
records.description: This study shows that amino acids facilitate microbial iron acquisition in environments that exhibit low nutrient concentration and where siderophores are highly diluted.

records.title: Probing the host cell exit strategy of Babesia divergens
records.description: This study uncovers druggable kinases and proteases required for host cell egress of the apicomplexan parasite Babesia divergens .

records.title: Varicella zoster virus and the central nervous system
